about: Math spans for LaTeX's own delimiters (mathdelimiters.ts): each case's math tokens in document order, as [type, content, markup, close] (a dollar token closes with its markup), with the parser's dollar math rules alongside (dollarmath.fixtures.json). \(...\) is inline math, \[...\] and the display environments are displayed math, as dollar math's tokens. A parser on the server, or a conversion of saved Markdown to the dollar form, must give the same spans. Within a paragraph, \[...\] is math when its content is padded with a space, a tab or a line feed just inside both brackets, or when it holds a command (a backslash and a letter), a brace, one of = + < >, or ^ or _ after its first character, a backslash before ASCII punctuation (a Markdown escape) and the character it escapes counting as neither; otherwise it is escaped brackets, which stay text. The content is read character by character, a line break as any other: a port must read it the same way, and any pattern it uses must match the whole content (Python: re.fullmatch, not re.match with ^...$, whose $ also matches before a final line feed). The last case comes from the tests of cscience-crypto, contributed under the MIT License by its author.
